issue.title: Timesync message warning spam
issue.body:
Continued from : https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/955

Summary

1 test program connected on TELEM1 with an FTDI cable to act as GroundStation
1 companion computer connected on TELEM2
AP is running using current PX4 beta firmware on master branch.
A Here2 GPS unit is connected.

GS receives the following message at a regular interval

` [12:02:24|Warn ] RTT too high for timesync: 1.57917e+12 ms`

CC receives the same message but sometimes with "1.57917e+12 ms" and sometimes a normal amount of time below 100ms

I don't know how to verify/set the time settings of the AP to see if it can fix the issue.

comments.body:
Please check if these messages appear again if:

1. GC connected, CC disconnected
2. CC connected, GC disconnected

Can you please tell which system time on CC and on GS PC during tests?

Here's the result, the test last 2 minutes.

Date on CC : Fri 24 Jan 09:49:52 UTC 2020
Date on GS : Fri 24 Jan 10:49:36 CET 2020

1. GC connected, CC disconnected

No message

2. CC connected, GC disconnected

No message

3. Both connected

On CC

```
[09:46:17|Warn ] RTT too high for timesync: 32.87 ms. (timesync.cpp:87)
[09:46:42|Warn ] RTT too high for timesync: 49.294 ms. (timesync.cpp:87)
[09:46:58|Warn ] RTT too high for timesync: 1.57986e+12 ms. (timesync.cpp:87)
[09:47:22|Warn ] RTT too high for timesync: 48.844 ms. (timesync.cpp:87)
[09:47:38|Warn ] RTT too high for timesync: 1.57986e+12 ms. (timesync.cpp:87)
```

On GS, 1 or 2 warnings every seconds.

`[10:47:55|Warn ] RTT too high for timesync: 1.57986e+12 ms. (timesync.cpp:87)`

Thank you!

Seems that:
1. On AP you have a not current UTC time but boot time.
2. `TIMESYNC` Messages from AP to CC and to GS have a one "extra hop":
2.1. `TIMESYNC` request    AP -> CC (`msg.tc1`: around 1970 (boot time), `msg.ts1`: 0)
2.2. `TIMESYNC` response CC -> AP (`msg.tc1`: around 1970 (boot time), `msg.ts1`: current CC time)
2.3. **Extra hop**:  
2.3.1. `TIMESYNC` *response (CC -> AP)*  AP -> GS (`msg.tc1`: around 1970 (boot time), `msg.ts1`: current CC time). 
3.3.2. Warning from GS every [10.Hz](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/1280351febf83591921dd48681ecaeae9c3d669e/src/modules/mavlink/mavlink_main.cpp#L1667) / [5 times skipping](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/develop/src/core/timesync.h#L30) == 2Hz from [this line ](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/develop/src/core/timesync.cpp#L87)

The same situation appears with CC, I think (are you use ROS on CC?).

I'm not familiar with MAVLink stack so it is complicate to me to say where is the problem and how you can solve it just now.

@julianoes may be you can help with message routing?
Seems that https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/pull/14016 related to this problem. It might fix this I suppose.
I need to look into the timesync stuff at some point. Right now I don't understand what it really does, so I rather not comment.

Just for help if you or something else will need to understand tymesync mechanism:

- MAVLink have an a simple message called [`TIMESYNC`](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#TIMESYNC):
It have only two fields:
 `ts1` - the one who needs (**Client**) to synchronize time with other side (**Server**) [put in this field his own time](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/develop/src/core/timesync.cpp#L29) (in nanoseconds)
 `tc1` - **Server** [put in this field his own current time](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/07d656e971a72d1202651dfd3b4642736fb078d7/src/modules/mavlink/mavlink_timesync.cpp#L66) in response message (see below).

- Algorithm of timesync in common words (**Client**: MAVSDK, **Server**: Autopilot):

1. **Client** [send](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/develop/src/core/timesync.cpp#L29) `TIMESYNC` message (request) with `tc1: 0; ts1: current_client_time`.
2. **Server** [receiving](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/07d656e971a72d1202651dfd3b4642736fb078d7/src/modules/mavlink/mavlink_timesync.cpp#L55) this message.
3. **Server** [create response TIMESYNC message](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/07d656e971a72d1202651dfd3b4642736fb078d7/src/modules/mavlink/mavlink_timesync.cpp#L64-L67) with `tc1: current_server_time; ts1: current_client_time`. `current_client_time` received in request message - **Server** [just make copy of it](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/07d656e971a72d1202651dfd3b4642736fb078d7/src/modules/mavlink/mavlink_timesync.cpp#L67)
4. **Server** [send response message](https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/blob/07d656e971a72d1202651dfd3b4642736fb078d7/src/modules/mavlink/mavlink_timesync.cpp#L69) to **Client**
5. **Client** receive `TIMESYNC` message and [see that](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/develop/src/core/timesync.cpp#L48) `tc1` is not eq `0`, so this is response message.
6. **Client** calculate time diff (`tc1 - ts1`) and [set time offset](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/develop/src/core/timesync.cpp#L51).
@depauwjimmy is this issue still actual or PX4/Firmware#14016 resolve it?
I think this is resolved unless when PX4 runs faster than realtime. For that case we can probably open a new issue.

issue.title: Timesync adjusting outgoing message timestamps

repository.name: MAVSDK
repository.description: API and library for MAVLink compatible systems written in C++ 20

issue.body:
The usual method for timesync with mavlink is that outgoing messages are sent with the sender's clock source, and the receiver should translate it into their own time frame. However, we've seen now with MAVSDK that after an initial timesync exchange it adjusts the clock source for _outgoing_ messages. This causes massive confusion on the flight controller side, since it was trying to adjust timestamps on incoming messages to what the clock source on MAVSDK was _before_ it did the timesync. This might be the root cause of #960 ? It can also cause instability in both timesync algorithms since they try to estimate each other when the offset is constantly changing, instead of estimating a single offset which should be mostly constant.

To fix this, outgoing messages should be timestamped with a consistent clock source (preferably CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW, ie something that isn't affected by time jumps or temporary clock slewing on the host system), and only incoming messages should be adjusted via the timesync message.

FYI @irsdkv , @JonasVautherin suggested I tag you since you contributed this. Do you see any problems here? Would you have time to fix this?

Thanks @DanielePettenuzzo for the investigation.

timeline.body: I think this is resolved unless when PX4 runs faster than realtime. For that case we can probably open a new issue.
